entry.note: Identified from the title page (arXiv:2605.20846v1, math.AT, 20 May 2026): Chris Li, 'Topological Field Theories and the Algebraic Structures of the Two-Sphere', 99 pp, 17 sections, thesis-style (the text calls itself a thesis; no institution on the extracted pages). No ref() entry existed. Entry li2026-two-sphere created 2026-09-06; no citation site yet.

relevance.rationale: The lead was the categorical-foundations chapter; the block that actually wants it is rem:tqft-context (folio/quantum-observable-universe/quantum-observable-universes/tqft-context.md), which asserts that the Frobenius–Hopf object A 'carries the 2d cobordism data' inside the 3d TQFT and that Hom(1, Ad(A)) = 0 is the 'categorical contact condition' for its irreducibility. Read: Introduction (Thms 1.0.3, 1.0.5–1.0.8), §5.1 (Def 5.1.1, Lemma 5.1.2, Def 5.1.7 P/L-monoids), §5.2 heading, §A.2. Thm 1.0.8 (= Thm 3.3.6) is the precise theorem behind the block's first sentence: a canonical isomorphism Cob(2) ≅ Cob(3)_{S^2,CF} between the 2d bordism category and the commutative-Frobenius sub-bordism category of the S^2-sector of Cob(3), sending n circles to n spheres and multiplication/unit/trace/comultiplication to their S^2 counterparts, a genus-g bordism to g connect-sum factors of S^2 × S^1. Thms 1.0.5/1.0.6 give the full presentation of Cob(3)_{S^2}: one extra generator per closed oriented irreducible prime 3-manifold (Kneser–Milnor, Thm 1.0.7) plus 'legs' relations; §5.1 packages a 3d TFT's Z(S^2) as a P-monoid ≅ L-monoid (commutative Frobenius monoid with prime-labelled units). Corpus-grep: 'Cob(' / 'bordism' occur in content/ only in this block (quantum-universes, quantum-observable-universes, models-of-qous: one hit); references.ts has the general TQFT frame (atiyah1988, kock2004, lurie2009, turaev2010) but no statement of the S^2-sector. Why 'supporting' and not 'core': Li's monoids are commutative and sit in a symmetric monoidal target; QOU's A is a Hopf algebra in a braided category and is not assumed commutative, so the match is at the Frobenius-structure level and does not identify A with Z(S^2) of any TFT. The prime-labelled units are extra structure the QOU axioms do not use. Scope-(a) on that: nothing here says the Hopf half or the braiding is incompatible with an S^2-sector reading — it is simply not addressed.

keyResults.statement: There is a canonical isomorphism S : Cob(2) → Cob(3)_{S^2,CF}; the commutative-Frobenius part of the S^2-sector of the 3d oriented bordism category is exactly the 2d cobordism category.
keyResults.useForFolio: Makes rem:tqft-context's 'A carries the 2d cobordism data' a cited theorem: for every 3d TFT, Z(S^2) is a commutative Frobenius monoid whose Frobenius data is Cob(2). Cite with the caveat that QOU's A is braided-Hopf, not assumed commutative.

keyResults.statement: Cob(3)_{S^2} is presented by commutative Frobenius generators plus one generator per closed oriented irreducible prime 3-manifold (a unit ∅ → S^2 or an endomorphism of S^2), subject to commutative-Frobenius and legs relations; P-monoids and L-monoids are in bijection.
keyResults.useForFolio: Names the structure the S^2-sector carries beyond Frobenius — prime-3-manifold-labelled units — which the QOU axioms do not use; a one-sentence remark in rem:tqft-context can record that scope honestly.
